chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Fuzalah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Zyad, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both).

He said: God the Blessed and Sublime revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): 'Do not rejoice in the abundance of wealth, and do not abandon remembering Me in any state, for the abundance of wealth causes forgetting of sins, and abandoning My remembrance hardens the hearts.'
ai.seo_question: How does wealth affect one's spiritual state according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this revelation to Musa (AS) to illustrate the dual spiritual hazards of materialism and spiritual neglect, emphasizing that wealth often causes *ghaflah* (heedlessness) while neglecting *dhikr* leads to *qasawat al-qalb* (hardening of the heart). This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that external abundance can obscure internal accountability, making constant remembrance essential for maintaining spiritual sensitivity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-23 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Fuzalat , on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad al-Sakoony, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that his father Al-Baqir (MGB) said, “The Blessed the Sublime God revealed to Moses (MGB), ‘Do not get pleased with the extent of your wealth and do not abandon remembering Me under any circumstances since extensive wealth will cause the forgetting of sins, and abandoning My remembrance will cause the hardening of hearts.’”
